title: Temporal Straightening for Latent Planning
claim: Pretrained encoders yield tangled, highly curved latent trajectories; our learned representation straightens them, making them separable and easier to plan in.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, original space then two PCA plots
description: Three panels in a row. The left panel, titled 'Original Space', shows a toy environment: a white square with a black wall and a gap in the middle. Blurred dotted trajectories in blue, orange and red-pink cross through the gap in an X-like pattern. The middle panel, 'PCA(DINO)', is a 2-D PCA scatter-line plot of the same trajectories encoded by a pretrained DINO encoder. The paths are jagged, tangled and overlapping, and they collapse into a cluster at the right. The right panel, 'PCA(Ours)', shows the trajectories encoded by the learned representation. They are smooth, nearly straight, evenly spaced and clearly separated, and they fan out from a shared center. The color coding is the same across all three panels. The eye goes first to the contrast between the messy middle plot and the clean right plot.
caption: Latent trajectories encoded by a pretrained visual encoder are usually highly curved, increasing the difficulty of prediction and planning. We learn a representation space where feasible trajectories are straighter to facilitate latent planning.
abstract: Learning good representations is essential for latent planning with world models. While pretrained visual encoders produce strong semantic visual features, they are not tailored to planning and contain information irrelevant -- or even detrimental -- to planning. Inspired by the perceptual straightening hypothesis in human visual processing, we introduce temporal straightening to improve representation learning for latent planning. Using a curvature regularizer that encourages locally straightened latent trajectories, we jointly learn an encoder and a predictor of a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world model. We show that reducing curvature this way makes the Euclidean distance in latent space a better proxy for the geodesic distance and improves the conditioning of the planning objective. We demonstrate empirically that temporal straightening makes gradient-based planning more stable and yields significantly higher success rates across a suite of goal-reaching tasks. Our code is available at https://agenticlearning.ai/temporal-straightening.
